exercises.prompt: With `Book`, `Book.age` and `achebe` defined as in the lesson, what is `{ achebe with year := 1959 }.age 2026`?

feedback.message: Not yet. That is `achebe.age 2026`; the updated copy has a different year.

hints: The `with` expression is a copy of `achebe` whose `year` is 1959.
exercises.solution: The copy has `year := 1959`, so its age in 2026 is `2026 - 1959 = 67`. `achebe` itself still has year 1958.

exercises.prompt: Using the robot program from the lesson, a robot starts at the default position (0, 0) facing north and follows `[.turnLeft, .forward 4, .turnLeft, .forward 1]`. Where does it end? Answer as `(x, y)`.
hints: Turning left from north faces west.
Turning left from west faces south.
exercises.solution: Turn left: facing west. Forward 4: `x` goes from 0 to -4. Turn left again: facing south. Forward 1: `y` goes from 0 to -1. The robot ends at `(-4, -1)`, facing south.

exercises.prompt: What does `Shape.name (.rectangle 5 5)` return? (Quotation marks are optional.)
hints: Look at the second line of the `match` in `name`.
exercises.solution: The value matches `rectangle w h` with `w = 5` and `h = 5`; since `w == h`, the result is `"square"`.

exercises.prompt: Using the `Tree` from the lesson, what is `([10, 20, 30, 40].foldl Tree.insert .leaf).depth`?

feedback.message: Not yet. Draw the tree: each new key is larger than everything before it, so where does it go?
Not yet. That would be the depth of a balanced tree with 4 keys, but this insertion order does not produce one.

hints: Insert the keys one at a time and draw the tree.
Each key is larger than all earlier ones, so it always goes to the right.
exercises.solution: Inserting keys in increasing order sends each one to the right of the last, so the tree is a chain 10 → 20 → 30 → 40 with depth 4. (The order `[30, 10, 40, 20]` gives depth 3.) This is why practical search trees rebalance themselves.

exercises.solution: `find?` returns the first element that passes the test, wrapped in `some`: `some 8`. If no element passed, as with `(· > 9)`, it would return `none`.

exercises.prompt: You add a constructor `| hexagon (side : Float)` to `Shape` but do not change `Shape.area`. What happens?

options.label: Lean rejects `Shape.area` with a missing-cases error until you handle `hexagon`.
options.feedback: Yes. Every Lean function must return a value for every input, so a non-exhaustive match is an error.

options.label: The program compiles, and `area` of a hexagon crashes at run time.
options.feedback: Not yet. Lean does not compile functions that are undefined for some inputs.

options.label: The program compiles, and `area` of a hexagon returns 0.
options.feedback: Not yet. Lean never invents a result for a missing case; that would be a silent bug.

options.label: Lean prints a warning but compiles the program.
options.feedback: Not yet. Some languages warn about non-exhaustive matches; in Lean it is an error.

hints: Remember the error the lesson showed for `Dir.right`.
exercises.solution: Lean reports `Missing cases:` followed by the unhandled pattern, and refuses the definition. That is a feature: adding a constructor makes the compiler list every function that needs a decision about it, provided those functions do not hide it behind a catch-all `_`.

exercises.prompt:
Which of these are valid definitions of a `Book`, as declared in the lesson? List their letters.

- A: `{ author := "Jane Austen", title := "Pride and Prejudice", year := 1813 }`
- B: `⟨"Pride and Prejudice", "Jane Austen", 1813, false⟩`
- C: `{ title := "Pride and Prejudice", year := 1813 }`
- D: `Book.mk "Pride and Prejudice" "Jane Austen" 1813 false`
- E: `⟨"Jane Austen", "Pride and Prejudice", "1813"⟩`
hints: Named fields may come in any order; only fields with defaults may be left out.
The anonymous constructor is positional, needs every field, and checks each field's type.
exercises.solution: **A, B and D.** A names its fields (order does not matter) and leaves out `onLoan`, which has a default. B and D give all four fields in order, B with the anonymous constructor and D with `Book.mk` directly. C is missing `author`, which has no default. E is wrong three times over: the anonymous constructor needs all four fields (defaults do not apply to it), the author and title are swapped, and the year is a string.
